title: Urbanisation and transport
description: Words for city growth, housing, congestion, public transport and urban planning, useful for Task 2 and map descriptions.

words.definition: the process of more people moving from the countryside to live in cities
words.example: Rapid urbanisation has put enormous pressure on housing in Asian cities.

words.definition: a situation in which roads are too full of traffic
words.example: A congestion charge has reduced traffic in central London.

words.definition: the uncontrolled spread of a city into the surrounding countryside
words.example: Urban sprawl increases car dependence because homes are far from workplaces.

words.definition: a person who travels regularly between home and work
words.example: Thousands of commuters travel into Jakarta from satellite towns every morning.

words.definition: to close a street to traffic so that only people walking can use it
words.example: The main shopping street was pedestrianised in 2015, and businesses have benefited.

words.definition: the connected system of buses, trains and other shared transport in an area
words.example: An efficient public transport network is essential for a growing city.

words.definition: homes that people on average or low incomes can pay for
words.example: The shortage of affordable housing forces many young people to live far from the centre.

words.definition: with too many people in a place
words.example: Overcrowded trains during rush hour make commuting uncomfortable.

words.definition: a very poor, crowded area of a city with bad housing
words.example: Many rural migrants end up living in slums on the edge of the city.

words.definition: useful facilities such as shops, parks and sports centres
words.example: New housing estates often lack basic amenities such as schools and clinics.

words.definition: describing a very tall building with many floors
words.example: High-rise apartments allow more people to live on less land.

words.definition: an area where people live on the edge of a city
words.example: Families often move to the suburbs to find larger, cheaper homes.

words.definition: the change of a poor area as richer people move in and prices rise
words.example: Gentrification has pushed many long-term residents out of the old town.

words.definition: the busy times of day when people travel to and from work
words.example: Delivery lorries should be banned from the city centre during rush hour.

words.definition: a part of a road reserved for bicycles
words.example: Building protected cycle lanes encourages more people to cycle to work.

words.definition: a situation in which people have to use cars because there are few other options
words.example: Poor bus services in suburban areas increase car dependence.

words.definition: the money you pay to travel on a bus, train or plane
words.example: Lower fares would encourage more drivers to switch to public transport.

words.definition: to give new life and energy to an area
words.example: The old harbour was revitalised with cafés, galleries and a waterfront park.

words.definition: having a lot of people living in a small area
words.example: Java is one of the most densely populated islands in the world.

words.definition: an area of grass, trees or plants in a town
words.example: Access to green space improves residents' physical and mental health.

words.definition: the official control of how land in different areas can be used
words.example: Strict zoning laws prevent factories from being built near schools.

words.definition: to move to a new place
words.example: The government plans to relocate the capital to reduce pressure on Jakarta.

words.definition: a road built around a town to keep traffic out of the centre
words.example: A new ring road was constructed to divert lorries away from the centre.

words.definition: a very large and busy city
words.example: Within fifty years, the small port had grown into a bustling metropolis.

words.definition: full of busy activity and people
words.example: The market is at its most bustling early in the morning.

words.definition: describing services that let people book a car or motorbike ride through an app
words.example: Ride-hailing apps have changed how people travel short distances in Indonesian cities.

words.definition: the movement of large numbers of people away from the countryside
words.example: The rural exodus has left many villages with mainly elderly residents.

words.definition: a main road in a town, used by a lot of traffic
words.example: The narrow lane became a busy thoroughfare after the new bridge opened.

words.definition: a fast, high-capacity rail system in a city
words.example: Jakarta's mass rapid transit system has cut journey times for thousands of commuters.

words.definition: pleasant and suitable to live in
words.example: Vienna regularly tops rankings of the world's most liveable cities.
